day_by_day.morning: No activities — flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities — flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Rome Fiumicino Airport at 22:30. Take the Leonardo Express train to Roma Termini (€14, ~32 min), then connect by bus or metro to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, freshen up, and get settled. Pick up a map and plan the week ahead.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or at the airport
meals.lunch: On the plane or at the airport
meals.dinner: Grab a quick late-night slice of pizza al taglio near Termini station (€2–4) — many spots stay open late for arriving travelers

day_by_day.notes: Keep arrival light — no sightseeing tonight. Validate your transport ticket on the Leonardo Express. Have €20–30 cash handy for incidentals. Rest well for a full day tomorrow.

day_by_day.morning: Slow start with breakfast near the hotel. Walk or take a short bus ride to explore the neighborhood around your accommodation. Stroll along the Tiber River banks for free scenic views and get oriented with the city layout. Visit the free exterior of Castel Sant'Angelo and snap photos from the iconic Ponte Sant'Angelo bridge.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the Vatican area for the Vatican Museums & Sistine Chapel experience. Book tickets online in advance to skip the line (€17–20 with online booking). Spend 3–4 hours marveling at the world's greatest art collection, including the Gallery of Maps, Raphael Rooms, and Michelangelo's breathtaking Sistine Chapel ceiling. Finish with a peek inside St. Peter's Basilica, which is free to enter.
day_by_day.evening: Wander through the charming Prati neighborhood near the Vatican for a relaxed evening stroll. Browse local shops and enjoy the lively atmosphere before heading back to the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Grab a cornetto and cappuccino at a local bar near the hotel (€2–3) — stand at the counter for the authentic Roman price
meals.lunch: Picnic-style lunch from a nearby alimentari (deli) — buy fresh bread, local cheese, cured meats, and fruit for under €8
meals.dinner: Trattoria da Lucia or a similar no-frills trattoria in Prati — try cacio e pepe or carbonara pasta (€10–14 for a full meal with house wine)

day_by_day.notes: Vatican Museums are closed on Sundays (except last Sunday of the month when entry is free but very crowded). Book tickets at least 2–3 days in advance online to avoid long queues. Dress code applies — cover shoulders and knees.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Borghese Gallery Art Tour — one of Rome's most stunning galleries housing Bernini's extraordinary sculptures and Caravaggio masterpieces. Admission is €13 and entry is strictly by timed reservation (book well in advance as slots fill up fast). Arrive early for your slot and spend 2 hours immersed in Baroque art. The surrounding Villa Borghese gardens are free and perfect for a post-gallery stroll.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or take a short bus ride to the Spanish Steps (free) and toss a coin at the Trevi Fountain (free to visit). Explore the elegant Piazza Navona, admiring Bernini's Fountain of the Four Rivers at no cost. Browse the free street art and architecture of the historic center.
day_by_day.evening: Join the Trastevere Food & Wine Evening Walk — wander through cobblestone streets sampling local Roman street food including supplì (fried rice balls), carciofi alla romana, and local wines. A guided food walk costs approximately €35–45 but covers multiple tastings, making it excellent value for a food lover.

meals.breakfast: Cornetto and cappuccino at a local bar near the hotel (€2–3)
meals.lunch: Street food near Piazza Navona — try a supplì from Supplì Roma or a simple pizza bianca (€3–5)
meals.dinner: Covered by the Trastevere Food & Wine Evening Walk tastings — supplement with a glass of house wine at a Trastevere enoteca if still hungry (€3–5)

day_by_day.notes: Borghese Gallery limits visitors to 2-hour timed slots — book as early as possible, ideally weeks ahead. The Trastevere walk typically runs in the evening starting around 18:30–19:00; confirm booking times in advance. Wear comfortable walking shoes for cobblestones.

day_by_day.morning: Early start for the Palatine Hill & Roman Forum Exploration. Purchase a combined ticket (€16) which also includes the Colosseum — valid for 24 hours. Spend the morning walking through the ancient heart of the Roman Empire, exploring the ruins of the Forum, the Palatine Hill palaces, and soaking in 2,000 years of history. Arrive by 9:00 AM to beat the midday heat and crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Use your combined ticket to visit the Colosseum in the afternoon. Book a timed entry slot online to avoid queues. Marvel at the iconic amphitheater from both outside and inside. Afterward, explore the Circus Maximus (free to walk around) and the nearby Aventine Hill for the famous Knights of Malta keyhole view of St. Peter's dome — completely free.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll through the vibrant Testaccio neighborhood, Rome's traditional working-class district and foodie heaven. Visit the Testaccio Market area and enjoy the local atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Bar snack near the hotel — cornetto and espresso (€2–3)
meals.lunch: Grab a quick panino or pizza al taglio near the Colosseum area (€4–6) — avoid sit-down restaurants in this tourist-heavy zone to save money
meals.dinner: Testaccio is famous for offal-based Roman cuisine — try Flavio al Velavevodetto or Da Remo pizzeria for an authentic, affordable Roman meal (€12–16 including a beer or wine)

day_by_day.notes: The combined Forum/Palatine/Colosseum ticket is best value. Book all slots online at coopculture.it to avoid the infamous queues. Start the Forum early as it gets very hot and crowded by midday. Bring water and sunscreen.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the lesser-known but stunning Capitoline Museums (€15) — the world's oldest public museums, sitting atop Capitoline Hill with panoramic views over the Roman Forum. See the original Marcus Aurelius equestrian statue, Caravaggio paintings, and ancient Roman sculptures. Spend 2–3 hours here for a deep dive into Roman and Renaissance art.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to the nearby Campo de' Fiori market (free to browse, runs until ~14:00) for local color, fresh produce, and cheap snacks. Then explore the Jewish Ghetto neighborhood — one of Rome's oldest and most atmospheric districts. Visit the free exterior of the Portico d'Ottavia ruins and browse the area. Head to the Pantheon (€5 entry) for a late afternoon visit — the 2,000-year-old temple is awe-inspiring.
day_by_day.evening: Free evening to revisit favorite neighborhoods or relax at the hotel. Consider a sunset stroll along the Tiber River.

meals.breakfast: Cornetto and cappuccino at a local bar (€2–3)
meals.lunch: Campo de' Fiori area — grab fresh fruit, olives, and a focaccia from market stalls (€5–7) for a budget picnic in the piazza
meals.dinner: Jewish Ghetto cuisine — try carciofi alla giudia (Jewish-style fried artichokes) and pasta at a local trattoria in the Ghetto (€12–15). Or cook a simple meal with market ingredients if your accommodation has kitchen access.

day_by_day.notes: Campo de' Fiori market closes by early afternoon on weekdays — aim to arrive by 13:00. The Pantheon now charges a small entry fee; arrive early or late afternoon to avoid peak crowds. The Capitoline Museums are closed on Mondays.

day_by_day.morning: Take a half-day trip to the nearby neighborhood of Ostiense to see the free street art district and the Centrale Montemartini museum (€7.50) — a fascinating former power plant displaying ancient Roman sculptures against industrial machinery. A truly unique and budget-friendly art experience off the beaten tourist path.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to central Rome and spend the afternoon exploring the Piazza del Popolo area (free). Visit the twin Baroque churches and the free Santa Maria del Popolo church containing two Caravaggio masterpieces. Climb the Pincian Hill terrace for sweeping free panoramic views over Rome's rooftops — one of the best free viewpoints in the city.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Trastevere for a self-guided evening stroll through its charming medieval streets, now familiar from Day 3. Sit in Piazza di Santa Maria in Trastevere and enjoy the atmosphere around the beautiful illuminated fountain and basilica (free to enter).

meals.breakfast: Cornetto and cappuccino at a local bar near the hotel (€2–3)
meals.lunch: Ostiense area — try a local pizza al taglio spot or a neighborhood bar for a budget panino (€4–6)
meals.dinner: Trastevere trattoria — try Da Enzo al 29 or similar for classic Roman dishes like rigatoni alla amatriciana or saltimbocca (€13–17 for a full meal)

day_by_day.notes: Centrale Montemartini is a hidden gem that most tourists miss — highly recommended for art lovers. Santa Maria del Popolo is often overlooked but contains two of Caravaggio's greatest works. Trastevere gets lively in the evening — great for people-watching.

day_by_day.morning: Last morning in Rome — revisit any favorites or explore the free Basilica di San Giovanni in Laterano (Rome's official cathedral, often overlooked by tourists) and its stunning cloisters (€3). Nearby, see the free Scala Santa (Holy Stairs) and the ancient Lateran Obelisk. A peaceful and authentic way to spend a final Roman morning away from tourist crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head back toward the hotel to collect luggage and begin departure preparations. Do any last-minute souvenir shopping at Campo de' Fiori or Porta Portese market (Sundays only) — avoid airport and tourist-trap shops for better prices. Stock up on affordable Italian gifts: local olive oil, pasta, or limoncello from a supermarket (Conad or Carrefour) for the best prices.
day_by_day.evening: Depart for the airport or transfer to your next destination. Take the Leonardo Express from Roma Termini to Fiumicino Airport (€14). Arrive at the airport at least 2.5 hours before your flight.

meals.breakfast: Final Roman breakfast at a local bar — savor one last cornetto and cappuccino standing at the counter (€2–3)
meals.lunch: Light lunch near the hotel or a takeaway supplì and pizza al taglio for a proper Roman farewell meal (€5–8)
meals.dinner: Airport dining if departing in the evening, or an early dinner near Termini station before heading to the airport — try a simple pasta at a neighborhood trattoria (€10–13)

day_by_day.notes: Allow extra time for the journey to the airport during evening rush hour. Keep €14–15 cash or card ready for the Leonardo Express. Supermarkets near Termini (Carrefour Express) are great for last-minute affordable food souvenirs. Double-check flight details and terminal information the night before.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival day — no morning activities scheduled. Flight UA lands at 22:30.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrival day — no afternoon activities scheduled.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Fiumicino Airport at 22:30. Clear customs, collect luggage, and take the Leonardo Express train or a pre-booked private transfer to central Rome (~45 min). Check in to Aegean Bliss Resort and settle into your room. Take a short stroll nearby if energy allows.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or at the airport.
meals.lunch: On the plane or at the airport.
meals.dinner: Grab a late-night bite near the hotel — look for a neighborhood trattoria or a late-opening pizzeria al taglio (pizza by the slice) for a quick, affordable Roman welcome meal.

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light. Confirm hotel check-in arrangements in advance given the late arrival time. Pre-book airport transfer to avoid taxi queues at night. Exchange currency or use ATMs at the airport.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely hotel breakfast to recover from travel. Afterwards, take a slow walk to explore the immediate neighborhood around the resort, get oriented, and pick up a local map or SIM card. Visit a nearby café for a classic Roman espresso and cornetto experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the Palatine Hill & Roman Forum Exploration. Spend 3–4 hours walking through the ancient heart of the Roman Empire — the ruins of the Forum, the Palatine Hill, and the sweeping views of the Colosseum exterior. Purchase combined tickets online in advance to skip queues.
day_by_day.evening: Wander into the nearby Testaccio neighborhood, one of Rome's most authentic food districts. Browse the Testaccio Market (if still open) and enjoy a relaxed dinner at a local trattoria.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a neighborhood café — try a cornetto and cappuccino (€3–5).
meals.lunch: Grab a casual lunch near the Roman Forum area — try a panino or suppli from a nearby bar or rosticceria (€8–12).
meals.dinner: Trattoria Da Remo or a similar mid-range spot in Testaccio — classic Roman dishes like cacio e pepe, coda alla vaccinara, and house wine (€25–35 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes — the Forum and Palatine Hill involve uneven cobblestones and significant walking. Bring water and sunscreen as June afternoons can be very warm. Book Forum/Palatine tickets online at least a day ahead.

day_by_day.morning: Vatican Museums & Sistine Chapel tour. Arrive early (pre-book a timed entry ticket or guided tour) to beat the crowds. Spend the morning exploring the vast papal art collections, Egyptian antiquities, the Gallery of Maps, and culminate in Michelangelo's awe-inspiring Sistine Chapel ceiling.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the Vatican, cross the Tiber and explore the charming Prati neighborhood for lunch. Then visit St. Peter's Basilica (free entry, separate queue from the Museums) and climb the dome for panoramic views of Rome. Stroll along the Castel Sant'Angelo riverside.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy the Trastevere Food & Wine Evening Walk — wander cobblestone streets sampling Roman street food including supplì, artichokes, porchetta, and local wines with a knowledgeable guide.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — fuel up before a full Vatican morning.
meals.lunch: Prati neighborhood near the Vatican — try Pizzarium Bonci for world-class pizza al taglio (€12–15), a local favorite and excellent mid-range value.
meals.dinner: Included as part of the Trastevere Food & Wine Evening Walk — various tastings of Roman street food and wine throughout the tour.

day_by_day.notes: The Vatican Museums require advance booking — do this as early as possible as slots fill weeks ahead, especially in June. Dress code enforced: covered shoulders and knees required for the Sistine Chapel and St. Peter's. The evening food walk typically lasts 2.5–3 hours.

day_by_day.morning: Traditional Roman Cooking Class. Join a hands-on morning session in a local chef's kitchen. Learn to make authentic Roman pasta dishes such as cacio e pepe, carbonara, or amatriciana, plus a dessert like tiramisu. A wonderful immersive experience combining art, culture, and food.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the class (and likely a hearty tasting lunch included), head to the Piazza Navona area. Explore the baroque square, admire Bernini's Fountain of the Four Rivers, and duck into the nearby Sant'Agnese in Agone church. Browse artisan shops and galleries in the surrounding streets.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll to the Pantheon (evening exterior viewing is free and magical), then explore the Campo de' Fiori market square — lively with locals in the evening. Enjoy a relaxed dinner nearby.

meals.breakfast: Light hotel breakfast before the cooking class.
meals.lunch: Tasting lunch is typically included as part of the cooking class experience.
meals.dinner: Restaurant near Campo de' Fiori or Piazza Navona — try Osteria dell'Ingegno or a similar mid-range osteria for Roman classics and local wine (€28–38 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Confirm whether the cooking class includes a lunch tasting — most do. Book the class in advance as spots are limited. The afternoon is intentionally lighter to balance the active morning.

day_by_day.morning: Borghese Gallery Art Tour. Visit one of Rome's most stunning galleries housing Bernini's extraordinary sculptures (Apollo and Daphne, The Rape of Proserpina) and Caravaggio's dramatic paintings. Entry is strictly timed (2-hour slots) — book well in advance. The gallery is set within the beautiful Villa Borghese gardens.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the gallery, enjoy a leisurely walk through the Villa Borghese gardens — rent a rowboat on the lake, visit the terrace viewpoint at Pincio for sweeping views over Rome's rooftops and domes, then descend the Spanish Steps and explore the upscale Via Condotti area.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the Trevi Fountain at dusk (less crowded than midday) — toss a coin and soak in the baroque spectacle. Then explore the Quirinale neighborhood for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a nearby café.
meals.lunch: Picnic in the Villa Borghese gardens — pick up fresh bread, cheese, cured meats, and fruit from a nearby alimentari or the Mercato Trionfale (€10–15 per person). A perfect mid-range, local experience.
meals.dinner: Mid-range restaurant near the Trevi Fountain or Quirinale — try Il Matriciano or similar for classic Roman cuisine (€28–35 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Borghese Gallery MUST be booked in advance — entry is capped at 360 visitors per 2-hour slot and sells out weeks ahead in summer. Arrive 15 minutes early. The gallery does not allow bags larger than A4 size inside.

day_by_day.morning: Free morning to revisit favorite spots or explore areas not yet seen. Options include: the Jewish Ghetto and its historic synagogue, the Aventine Hill's famous keyhole view of St. Peter's dome through the Knights of Malta garden, or the peaceful Orange Garden (Giardino degli Aranci) with panoramic views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Capitoline Museums (the world's oldest public museums) on Capitoline Hill — housing Marcus Aurelius's bronze equestrian statue, the Capitoline Wolf, and stunning views of the Roman Forum from the terrace. A great complement to the Forum visit earlier in the week.
day_by_day.evening: Splurge slightly on a special farewell-style dinner at a well-regarded Roman restaurant. Explore the Pigneto or Ostiense neighborhoods for a more local, less touristy Saturday night atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast.
meals.lunch: Casual lunch in the Jewish Ghetto — try the famous fried artichokes alla giudia and baccalà at a local trattoria (€15–20 per person).
meals.dinner: A slightly elevated mid-range dinner — try Flavio al Velavevodetto in Testaccio or Roscioli near Campo de' Fiori for exceptional Roman cuisine and natural wines (€35–45 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Saturday in Rome is lively — markets, locals shopping, and a festive atmosphere. The Capitoline Museums are less crowded than the Vatican but still worth booking online. The Aventine keyhole is free and a hidden gem — arrive early to avoid a queue.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Porta Portese flea market (open Sunday mornings until 2pm) — one of Rome's largest and most famous outdoor markets, great for vintage finds, antiques, art prints, and local atmosphere. Stroll through Trastevere in the morning when it's quieter and photogenic.
day_by_day.afternoon: Final afternoon at leisure — return to a favorite piazza, do last-minute souvenir shopping (look for quality prints, ceramics, or food items like pasta, olive oil, and truffles), or visit any remaining sites on your wish list. Pack and prepare for departure.
day_by_day.evening: Early dinner before heading to the airport or resting at the hotel. Keep it simple and satisfying — a final Roman pizza or pasta at a neighborhood spot.

meals.breakfast: A special Sunday breakfast — try a local bar in Trastevere for fresh pastries and a proper cappuccino, enjoyed standing at the counter like a true Roman (€4–6).
meals.lunch: Light lunch in Trastevere after the market — try Da Enzo al 29 or a similar beloved neighborhood trattoria (€20–28 per person).
meals.dinner: Simple, satisfying farewell meal near the hotel — a classic Roman pizzeria or neighborhood trattoria (€18–25 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Porta Portese gets very busy by 10am — arrive by 9am for the best experience. Keep valuables secure in the market crowds. Confirm checkout time with the hotel and arrange luggage storage if your flight is in the evening. Rome's Fiumicino Airport recommends arriving 2.5–3 hours before international flights.

Visit the Testaccio Market for a curated food tasting tour: fresh buffalo mozzarella, supplì al telefono, artisan cured meats, and local cheeses. Spend the late afternoon at leisure — perhaps a spa treatment at the hotel.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Roscioli Ristorante Salumeria — one of Rome's most lauded gourmet destinations, celebrated for its extraordinary wine cellar (2,700+ labels) and exquisite Roman-Jewish cuisine. Book the chef's tasting menu with full wine flight.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — smoked salmon, avocado toast, freshly squeezed juices, cappuccino
meals.lunch: Gourmet market tasting in Testaccio — artisan bites, local cheeses, supplì, and a glass of chilled Vermentino
meals.dinner: Chef's tasting menu at Roscioli with sommelier-led wine flight — a true Roman culinary institution

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes for the Forum — cobblestones and uneven terrain throughout. Book Roscioli dinner reservation at least 3–4 weeks ahead; it is perpetually in demand. SPF and a hat are strongly recommended for the open-air ancient sites in June.

day_by_day.morning: Dedicated morning of leisurely cultural exploration — visit the Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Antica at Palazzo Barberini, housing Raphael's La Fornarina and Hans Holbein's Henry VIII. A private docent guide provides an exclusive, unhurried experience. Afterwards, admire the Baroque masterpiece of the Trevi Fountain (best visited mid-morning before peak crowds).
day_by_day.afternoon: Private transfer to Trastevere for an afternoon of wandering through its photogenic medieval lanes. Explore the golden mosaics of the Basilica di Santa Maria in Trastevere. Browse independent boutiques and artisan studios. Relax at a shaded café terrace with an Aperol Spritz and Roman snacks.
day_by_day.evening: Trastevere Food & Wine Evening Walk — a curated guided evening stroll through Trastevere's cobblestone streets, sampling local Roman street food including supplì, carciofi alla giudia, porchetta, and artisan gelato, paired with natural wines and craft beers at atmospheric wine bars and enotecas.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — eggs any style, Roman pastries, granola, fresh-pressed orange juice
meals.lunch: Leisurely lunch at Glass Hostaria Trastevere — a Michelin-recognized restaurant with creative Roman-inspired cuisine and a stunning wine list
meals.dinner: Progressive food and wine evening walk through Trastevere — multiple tastings across 4–5 stops

day_by_day.notes: The Trastevere food walk typically runs 2.5–3 hours starting at sunset (around 20:00 in June). Wear comfortable shoes. Palazzo Barberini is closed on Mondays — confirm opening day when booking.

day_by_day.morning: Exclusive day trip to the Castelli Romani — the volcanic hill towns south of Rome. Private chauffeured car takes you to Frascati, the wine capital of Lazio, for a private winery tour and barrel tasting at a historic estate. Explore the elegant Villa Aldobrandini gardens with sweeping views over Rome.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to the medieval hilltop town of Castel Gandolfo — the Pope's summer residence — for a private tour of the Papal Gardens and Astronomical Observatory. Stroll the lakeside promenade of Lake Albano and enjoy the tranquil countryside atmosphere far from the city's bustle.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Rome in time for a sunset cocktail on a rooftop bar — Il Sorpasso Rooftop or Hotel Eden's La Terrasse Cuisine offer unmatched panoramic views. Follow with an intimate dinner at La Pergola, Rome's only 3-Michelin-star restaurant, for an extraordinary tasting menu by Chef Heinz Beck.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — continental spread with local honey, ricotta, seasonal berries, and espresso
meals.lunch: Estate lunch at the Frascati winery — seasonal farm-to-table antipasti, house-made pasta, and wine pairings in a private vineyard setting
meals.dinner: La Pergola — Rome's pinnacle of fine dining; 3-Michelin-star tasting menu (10 courses) with full wine pairing by the sommelier

day_by_day.notes: La Pergola reservation is essential — book 4–6 weeks in advance. Smart dress code required (jacket for gentlemen). The winery day trip should be pre-arranged through the hotel concierge for a seamless private experience.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Rome — enjoy a long, indulgent breakfast at the hotel. Take a private stroll or short transfer to the Pantheon for a quiet early-morning visit (opens at 09:00) — one of the world's best-preserved ancient buildings, now even more magnificent after its recent restoration. Pause at Caffè Sant'Eustachio nearby for what many consider Rome's finest espresso.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the hotel for checkout. Depending on departure time, enjoy a final light lunch at the hotel's restaurant or a nearby trattoria. Private luxury transfer to Rome Fiumicino Airport ensures a relaxed, stress-free departure.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Rome. Carry the memories of seven extraordinary days of art, history, and gastronomy.

meals.breakfast: Grand farewell breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort — full spread with Roman pastries, eggs, charcuterie, fresh juices, and specialty coffees
meals.lunch: Light farewell lunch — Roman supplì, crostini, and a final glass of Frascati at a café near the Pantheon or at the hotel
meals.dinner: In-flight or at the airport

day_by_day.notes: Arrange late checkout with the hotel if your flight departs in the evening — most luxury hotels accommodate this with advance notice. Allow at least 3 hours before international departure for airport transfer and check-in. Consider purchasing artisan food gifts (pasta, olive oil, wine) at a gourmet shop near the Pantheon before heading to the airport.
